In 1942, the Polish army enlisted a bear.
Polish soldiers in Iran bought a tiny bear cub from a boy. They named him Wojtek, smiling warrior.
He drank milk from a vodka bottle. Later, he drank beer.
He wrestled with the soldiers, and even ate their cigarettes.
But in 1944, the unit had to sail to Italy, and pets were not allowed on the ship.
So the army made him a soldier. Private Wojtek, with a name, a number, and rations.
At the Battle of Monte Cassino, the guns needed shells.
According to the soldiers, Wojtek carried heavy ammunition crates for the gunners.
The unit changed its badge to a bear carrying a shell.
And Wojtek was promoted to corporal.
After the war, he retired to Edinburgh Zoo.
His old comrades visited, spoke to him in Polish, and some even climbed in to wrestle him.
